```python
def sum_of_unique_elements(sequence):
    seen = set()
    unique = []
    for num in sequence:
        if num not in seen:
            seen.add(num)
            unique.append(num)
        else:
            seen.discard(num)
    return sum(unique)
```

This code works by iterating over the input list, `sequence`. It maintains a set, `seen`, which keeps track of the numbers it has seen. When it encounters a number that has not been seen before, it adds it to both the `seen` set and the `unique` list. This means that every unique number will have only appeared once in both the `seen` and `unique` lists. Finally, it returns the sum of all elements in `unique`, which contain all unique elements from `sequence`.
